name: PCAL6416AHF,128
title: PCAL6416A: 16-bit I2C-bus/SMBus I/O expander with level translation, interrupt, reset and Agile I/O
summary: The PCAL6416A gives a microcontroller sixteen more general-purpose I/O pins, in two 8-bit ports, over a 400 kHz I2C-bus or SMBus. Bus side and port side have separate supplies, each 1.65 V to 5.5 V, so the part also shifts logic levels between the host and the peripherals. Besides direction, output and input inversion registers it has per-pin drive strength, input latching, 100 kΩ pull-up or pull-down resistors and interrupt masking, plus per-port open-drain outputs, an interrupt status register, an open-drain INT output, a RESET input and one address pin.
key_figures: VDD(I2C-bus) 1.65 V to 5.5 V; VDD(P) 1.65 V to 5.5 V
I2C-bus / SMBus, 0 to 400 kHz; address 0100 00x, ADDR pin
25 mA per I/O recommended; 100 mA per port, 200 mA device

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A master controller on a 1.8 V bus drives the expander, whose port runs from its own VDD(P) rail. SCL, SDA, INT and RESET each have a 10 kΩ pull-up to the 1.8 V bus supply, which also feeds VDD(I2C-bus). ADDR is grounded, so the slave address is 0100 000x. P0_0 reads the output of an alarm subsystem powered from VDD(P); P0_1 is an output driving the enable of a controlled switch. P0_2 to P1_0 are keypad inputs, each with an optional 10 kΩ pull-up to VDD(P), and P1_1 to P1_7 are outputs to the keypad.

Port inputs that can float take a resistor, fitted outside or the internal pull-up or pull-down; inputs held by their driver at all times take none.
Outputs in push-pull mode need no outside pull-up resistors; outputs in open-drain mode need them.

circuits.title: LED drive with a 100 kΩ resistor across the LED
circuits.description: A port pin sinks the current of an LED fed through a series resistor from the VDD(P) supply. A 100 kΩ resistor from the supply to the pin holds the pin near VDD(P) while the LED is dark, so no extra supply current flows.

parts.note: LED current-setting resistor; no value given

notes: P0_0 stands for any port pin Pn.

circuits.title: LED on 5 V with the device on 3.3 V
circuits.description: The expander runs from 3.3 V while its LED, with a series resistor, is fed from 5 V and sunk by a port pin. With VDD(P) at least 1.2 V under the LED supply, the pin sits at or above VDD(P) when the LED is off, which keeps IDD(P) from rising.

operation.text: VDD(I2C-bus) powers the bus side and VDD(P) powers the core and the 16 port pins; each may be anywhere from 1.65 V to 5.5 V, independently. Tie VDD(I2C-bus) to the supply of the master's SCL and SDA lines: it tells the part the bus logic level, while VDD(P) sets the port level.

The device has the four register pairs of the PCA6416A (input, output, polarity inversion, configuration) and the same pinout, so it drops into a PCA6416A footprint, and its software is backward compatible. On top it adds the Agile I/O registers: drive strength, input latch, pull-up/pull-down enable and select, interrupt mask, interrupt status and push-pull/open-drain output selection. Unlike the PCA6416A it starts with every interrupt masked, so no spurious interrupts appear while a board comes up.

An I2C-bus and SMBus slave, up to 400 kHz (Fast-mode). SCL and SDA have Schmitt-trigger inputs, so slow edges are tolerated, with typical hysteresis of 0.18 V at 1.8 V, 0.25 V at 2.5 V, 0.33 V at 3.3 V and 0.5 V at 5 V, and a noise filter that rejects spikes up to 50 ns. SCL is an input only.
The seven-bit slave address is 0100 00 followed by the level on ADDR, so two devices can share a bus. The eighth bit is R/W: HIGH reads, LOW writes. ADDR goes straight to VDD(P) or ground.

After the address is acknowledged, the master's next byte goes into the write-only pointer register and picks the register for the data that follows. The low three bits choose among the eight original registers; bit 6 set, with the low bits, reaches the Agile I/O registers at 40h to 4Fh.

The 22 registers work as 11 pairs, one byte for port 0 and one for port 1 (drive strength takes two pairs). After a data byte the pointer flips to the other register of the same pair, so writing 03h then a second byte puts the second byte in 02h. A write can carry any number of data bytes, the pointer alternating within the pair each time.

To read, the master writes the address and the command byte, sends a repeated START, then the address with R/W = 1. The device returns the chosen register, then its partner, alternating for as many bytes as the master acknowledges; the master leaves the last byte unacknowledged. The register takes its data at the rising edge of the acknowledge clock pulse. After a later repeated START, the read resumes at the other register of the pair from where it stopped.
Read-only images of the logic levels on the pins, whether a pin is an input or an output. Writing them does nothing; their power-up value is whatever the pins carry.
The levels driven onto pins set as outputs; they do not affect pins set as inputs. Reading them returns what was written, not the pin level. Default 1.
A 1 inverts the corresponding input pin's bit in the input register; a 0 leaves it as is. Default 0.
A 1 makes the pin a high-impedance input, a 0 an output. Default 1: every pin starts as an input.

Two bits per pin choose one quarter, one half, three quarters or all of the output stage: the setting switches in that many of four parallel transistor pairs (fingers) in both the pull-up and pull-down halves, so 10b runs two fingers and halves the drive. Weaker drive lowers the switching current peak in the VDD and VSS package inductance, which reduces the ground and supply bounce when many outputs switch together, and suits low-capacitance lines. Default 11b, full drive.

Applies only to pins set as inputs. With the latch bit 0, a change on the pin raises an interrupt, and if the pin returns to its first level before the input register is read, the interrupt goes away again. With the bit 1, the new level is captured in the input register and held, with the interrupt, until the input register is read, even if the pin has already gone back; the read returns the captured value and the next read returns the present level. Example: a latched P0_4 at 0 pulses to 1 and back; the first read of input port 0 shows bit 4 as 1 and clears the interrupt, the second shows 0. An interrupt stays asserted when a non-latched input changes together with a latched one and then returns; reading reflects only the latched change and clears the interrupt. Changing a bit from latched to non-latched does not clear a pending interrupt; afterwards a read shows the present pin level, and in the other direction a read shows the latched level. Default 0.

A 1 in the enable register connects a resistor to the pin; a 0 removes it. The selection register picks a pull-up (1) or a pull-down (0) of 100 kΩ typical, 50 kΩ minimum, 150 kΩ maximum; with the resistor disabled the selection bit has no effect. The resistors are also disconnected from pins whose port is set to open-drain. Enable defaults to 0, selection to 1.

All mask bits are 1 at power-on, so no input can assert INT during start-up. Clearing a bit to 0 lets that input assert INT. Clearing the mask of an input that has already changed asserts INT at once; setting the mask of the input currently causing an interrupt releases INT.
Read-only. A 1 marks an input that caused the interrupt, a 0 one that did not. The status bit of a masked input always reads 0. Default 0.

Bit 0 (ODEN0) sets the whole of port 0 and bit 1 (ODEN1) the whole of port 1: 0 is push-pull, with both the upper and lower transistors in use, 1 is open-drain, with only the lower transistor. Write this register before the configuration registers turn the pins into outputs. Default 0, push-pull.

As an input both output transistors are off and the pin is high impedance; it may be taken above VDD(P), up to 5.5 V, so the ports are 5 V tolerant. As an output one transistor connects the pin to VDD(P) or to VSS, following the output register, and the pin should then be kept within the recommended levels. Each pin has ESD diodes. A pin set as an output never causes an interrupt.

Rising from 0 V, VDD(P) holds the part in reset until it passes VPOR (1.1 V typical, 1.4 V maximum); then all registers take their defaults and the bus state machine starts. For another power-on reset VDD(P) must fall below VPOR and rise again: below 0.2 V (or to VSS), or to 50 mV under VPOR(min), and stay there at least 1 µs, with fall and rise rates inside the table limits. The trip point is 0.7 V or more on a falling supply and 1.4 V or less on a rising one. Short dips need not reset the part: a dip of up to 1.0 V lasting under 1 µs, or a dip to half of VDD(P) lasting up to 10 µs, causes no upset. Bypass capacitance, source impedance and device impedance all affect how the part rides through a dip. The outputs do not glitch at power-up.

Holding RESET LOW for at least tw(rst) (30 ns) puts all registers and the bus state machine back to their defaults without removing power. Once RESET is HIGH the port levels can change again. Without an active driver, RESET needs a pull-up to VDD(I2C-bus).

INT is open-drain and active LOW; pull it up to VDD(P) or VDD(I2C-bus), whichever supplies the device that takes the interrupt. Any rising or falling edge on an unmasked input asserts INT within tv(INT). For a non-latched input INT clears when the pin returns to its old level or when the port that caused it is read; for a latched input only the read clears it. The clearing happens at the ACK or NACK bit of the read, after SCL rises, so an input change during that clock pulse can be lost or give only a very short pulse; later changes are reported normally. Turning an output into an input can raise a false interrupt when the pin level differs from the input register.

The port outputs sink up to 25 mA each, enough to light an LED directly. An LED from VDD to a pin leaves the pin about 1.2 V under VDD(P) when the LED is off, and IDD(P) climbs as the pin voltage drops below VDD(P). Two ways keep the pin at or above VDD(P): a high-value resistor (100 kΩ) across the LED, or a VDD(P) at least 1.2 V lower than the LED supply.
Keep each I/O to 25 mA, each group of eight to 100 mA and the device to 200 mA of sink current (the VSS rating); the I/Os together may source at most 160 mA.

A power-on reset or RESET returns the part to its default state, at the cost of the port configuration. A STOP from the master puts the slave state machine in a known idle state with SDA released. If the master stops mid-transfer while the device is sending data or an acknowledge, SDA stays LOW and blocks the bus; the master can then send nine clocks on SCL, which always brings the device back to idle, the extra clocks being taken as STOP conditions. Since SCL is input-only on this part, a stuck LOW SCL comes from the master or from another slave stretching the clock.
The centre pad of the HWQFN24 is not a required connection. If it is soldered, it may connect only to ground, as a second ground; otherwise leave it open.
Latch-up above 100 mA to JESD 78 Class II; ESD above 2000 V HBM (JESD22-A114-A) and 1000 V CDM (JESD22-C101).

All five packages can be reflow soldered. The ball-grid packages and the HWQFN, with lands under the body, cannot be wave soldered. Leaded parts with a pitch under about 0.6 mm are not wave soldered either. Peak reflow temperature follows J-STD-020D by package thickness and volume; follow the moisture sensitivity handling given on the packing.
